purpose: What the product is, who it is for and how you will know it is working. Every other file defers to it on those three questions.

build.when: Run it first: every other file defers to it.
build.reads: The README, the package manifest, the routes, any plan, pricing or feature-flag configuration, the specs, the commit history, and any analytics the project names.
asks: What it is, in two or three sentences, and what people confuse it with
Who it is for, who else uses or buys it, and who it says no to
The problem it solves
Three to five success measures, and which cannot be measured yet
What exists, built from the code: it asks only what the code cannot show
Four to seven product principles, each ruling between two things
What people ask for that will not be built
What is still undecided

purpose: The rules for how the product looks, reads and behaves: visual system, UX principles, components, forms and accessibility. Anything a check could enforce lives here.
readNote: /ux-os:init offers it as a house rule, and /ux-os:run then holds third-party skills to it.

build.reads: The token files, the component catalog and its demos, the design-system docs, any design linter and its configuration, the shared form components and the accessibility tests.
asks: The brand in one line: what someone should feel, and must never feel
Colour roles, only where two tokens claim one or a role has none
The rules for type, spacing, radii, elevation and icons
Five to ten UX principles, each with what it rules out
How a new component gets added
Forms: labels, required fields, validation, errors, button order
The accessibility floor
Words on screen, which become a pointer to VOICE.md

purpose: The first file an AI coding agent reads: a pointer to the guides, plus the few rules that must not be missed. Never a second copy of the guide.
readNote: Most coding agents look for AGENTS.md by convention. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, so have one point at the other.

build.when: Run it last: it points at all the others.
build.reads: The agent guide (CLAUDE.md or its equivalent), any other agent instruction files, the CI configuration, the deploy scripts, the environment example, any agent hooks and the test commands.
asks: Which file is the guide
Which other files an agent must read, and when
The guardrails, where a mistake is expensive or hard to undo
What finished means here

purpose: Who the product is for, as people with situations, goals and frustrations. Beliefs until research backs them.
readNote: The ux-os research skills read it as beliefs once .research-profile.md lists it under Belief files.

build.reads: PRODUCT.md, the research profile and its research folder, any personas a research run wrote, and any analytics the profile names.
asks: The one behaviour that most changes what someone needs
At most four personas, placed on it
The primary persona, and why
For each: what would make them refuse, the least evidenced claim, and what would show the persona is wrong

purpose: How each primary persona gets the job done today, stage by stage, with where it hurts. Beliefs until research backs them.
readNote: The ux-os research skills read it as beliefs once .research-profile.md lists it under Belief files.

build.when: Run it after PERSONAS.md, whose personas it maps.
build.reads: PERSONAS.md, PRODUCT.md, the research folder and any journeys a research run wrote.
asks: Which journeys: one per primary persona
For each: the scenario, where it starts and ends, five to seven stages, and how each stage feels
Two or three moments that matter
Whether to add a future journey

purpose: The progress people are trying to make, independent of any product, and what they hire to make it today. Beliefs until research backs them.
readNote: The ux-os research skills read it as beliefs once .research-profile.md lists it under Belief files.

build.when: Run it after PERSONAS.md and JOURNEYS.md.
build.reads: PRODUCT.md, PERSONAS.md, JOURNEYS.md, the research folder and any jobs model a research run wrote.
asks: The core job, naming no product, and what sets it off
What has to get done, how customers want to feel, and how they want to be seen
The job map, four to eight stages
What gets hired today, including doing nothing, doing it by hand and hiring someone
Underserved outcomes, naming no solution
A job statement per persona
What each outcome asks of the product

purpose: The judgment no check can enforce: what to reason toward and away from, what reads as machine-made, and the kill list. DESIGN.md says what is allowed; this says what is good.

build.when: Run it after DESIGN.md, which holds the rules it must not repeat. The owner answers.
build.reads: DESIGN.md, any critiques, review notes or design-loop learnings the project keeps, and the file’s own dated notes.
asks: The root: what good means here, in two to five words
Reference anchors to reason toward and away from, each with its specific quality
The cut test: how a feature, section or element earns its place
Soul: the kind of delight allowed, and how much
What reads as machine-made
The kill list
Taste that is not settled yet

purpose: How things move: the feel in three words, the standard values as tokens, the allowed patterns, the banned ones and the reduced-motion rule.

build.reads: The motion tokens, the animation code, any motion docs in the design system, and every place the code handles reduced motion.
asks: Three words for how motion should feel, each with what it rules out
The standard values, only where the code and the file disagree
Five patterns or fewer, each with its values
What motion must never do
What changes when someone asks for less motion
The stack, and what is ruled out

purpose: How the product sounds in every word a user reads: the voice in one line, pillars with before and after, words to avoid and the shape of common messages.
readNote: No skill reads VOICE.md by name yet. /ux-os:init offers it as a house rule, so point AGENTS.md at it.

build.when: Run it after DESIGN.md and taste.md.
build.reads: The product’s own copy (buttons, errors, empty states, confirmations, emails), any writing style guide, the banned-word list and any copy linter.
asks: Scope: the words in the product only, or long-form too
The voice in one line
Three or four pillars, each with a real line that misses and its rewrite
What the voice is not
The words you never use
The shape of the messages written most: button, error, empty state, confirmation, waiting
Mechanics and inclusive language
